title: The relationship between stress, occupational burnout, and retirement intention Among 179 elite athletes.
abstract: BackgroundEarly retirement among elite athletes is prevalent, yet research remains limited on the occupational mental health of athletes in western China.ObjectiveThis study explores the relationships between stress, occupational burnout, and retirement intention among elite athletes in Sichuan Province, and verifies an indirect association model.MethodsStratified random sampling was employed to select 179 elite athletes from Sichuan Province. Surveys were conducted using the Athlete Stressor Questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI-Athlete version) and Athlete Retirement Intention Questionnaire.ResultsEmotional exhaustion was significantly positively correlated with depersonalisation (r = 0.423, p < 0.01) and negatively correlated with personal accomplishment (r = -0.386, p < 0.01). Hierarchical regression identified four key correlates of retirement intention: emotional exhaustion (β = 0.382), years of training (β = 0.205), personal accomplishment (β = -0.231) and age (β = 0.217). Together, these four variables explained 40.2% of the variance. Both training and competition stress and communication stress showed patterns consistent with full indirect association with retirement intention via emotional exhaustion and depersonalisation; the indirect pathways accounted for 97.3% and 83.3% of the total associations, respectively.ConclusionOccupational burnout acts as an indirect link between stress and retirement intention among elite Sichuan athletes, with emotional exhaustion as the core influencing factor. Communication stress showed stronger indirect associations with retirement intention than training and competition stress. Intervention strategies should be developed to alleviate emotional exhaustion, enhance personal accomplishment and improve communication mechanisms.

title: HuR Inhibition Attenuates Hypertension and Fibrosis in Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upregulation of the RNA-binding protein HuR (human antigen R) has been reported in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its pathogenic role remains incompletely understood. We hypothesized that HuR promotes renal and vascular injury in hypertensive CKD and that pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates disease progression. We therefore investigated the role of HuR in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) plus Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced CKD and evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the HuR inhibitor, KH3 .
METHODS: Male mice underwent uninephrectomy followed by DOCA+Ang II infusion with 1% NaCl in drinking water and were treated with KH3 or vehicle for 3 weeks. Control mice received saline without DOCA or Ang II.
RESULTS: DOCA+Ang II markedly increased HuR expression in circulating exosomes and kidney tissues, which was attenuated by KH3 treatment. KH3 reduced albuminuria, improved renal function, and attenuated kidney hypertrophy, glomerular, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. These renoprotective effects were associated with reduced podocyte and tubular injury, decreased macrophage infiltration, and suppression of NF-κB (nuclear factor-kappa B) p65, Nox2 (NADPH oxidase 2), AKT (protein kinase B) phosphorylation, TGFβ1 (transforming growth factor β1), and Wisp1 (WNT1-inducible signaling pathway protein 1) signaling. KH3 also partially lowered arterial blood pressure in DOCA+Ang II-treated mice. Further studies in vascular smooth muscle cells and mesenteric resistance arteries suggested that HuR inhibition may suppress vascular profibrotic signaling associated with SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2).
CONCLUSIONS: HuR is upregulated in renal and vascular tissues in DOCA+Ang II-induced CKD and contributes to renal inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and vascular dysfunction. Pharmacological inhibition of HuR attenuates renal and vascular injury, supporting HuR as a promising therapeutic target for CKD.

title: Aerobic exercise preconditioning enhances skeletal muscle resistance and recovery after contusion: involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compared with passive recovery after injury, exercise preconditioning may provide an active strategy for improving the subsequent response of skeletal muscle to injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of aerobic exercise preconditioning (AEP) on skeletal muscle injury (SMI) and post-injury repair, with particular focus on the involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and changes in PGC-1α acetylation.
METHODS: This study initially investigated the effects of continuous aerobic exercise on skeletal muscle in healthy mice. Subsequently, the influence of AEP on injury severity and regenerative repair of the gastrocnemius muscle was examined in mice with SMI. Western blotting was used to determine the expression levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α proteins, immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the acetylation status of PGC-1α, and qRT-PCR was used to analyze the expression of genes associated with mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers and muscle regeneration. Finally, the involvement of SIRT1 signaling in the AEP-associated response to SMI was further examined using the pharmacological SIRT1 inhibitor EX527.
RESULTS: Continuous aerobic exercise was associated with increased SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling and changes in mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers in the gastrocnemius muscle of healthy mice. AEP was associated with reduced injury-related changes and an improved post-injury repair profile in mice with SMI. During the early stage after injury, AEP was accompanied by sustained SIRT1/ PGC-1α signaling and reduced PGC-1α acetylation. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 with EX527 partially attenuated the AEP-associated protective and reparative effects on the injured gastrocnemius muscle.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that AEP establishes an adaptive state in skeletal muscle that is associated with reduced injury-related damage and an enhanced post-injury reparative response. The SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and altered PGC-1α acetylation may contribute to these AEP-associated effects.

title: Beyond Movement Behaviours: Unravelling the Prospective Links Between 24-Hour Behavioural Composition and Affective Dynamics in Adolescent Athletes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the full spectrum of 24-hour movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (SLP), sedentary behaviour (SB), light physical activity (LPA), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (S-MVPA), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (US-MVPA) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured MVPA subdomains on emotional outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). Accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. Four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (EMA): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. Bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect.
RESULTS: Associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. A higher relative proportion of LPA was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% Bayesian credible interval [CrI] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% CrI 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% CrI -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% CrI -0.236 to -0.185). In 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to LPA generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. These findings highlight LPA as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect.
CONCLUSIONS: Daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. LPA showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing SB. Promoting LPA may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands.

title: Exploring the Impact of Ovarian Hormones on Cortical Drive and Quadriceps Performance in Uninjured Female Athletes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian hormones fluctuate across the menstrual cycle (MC) and differ between oral contraceptive (OC) users and naturally menstruating (NM) individuals. Hormones may affect cortical drive to peripheral muscles through excitatory effects of estradiol and inhibitory effects of progesterone on the central nervous system. The impact of hormones on cortical drive is poorly understood. This study aimed to (1) determine the effects of MC phase and OC use on cortical drive and quadriceps performance and (2) determine the relationship between ovarian hormones and these outcomes. We hypothesized that cortical drive will differ between MC phases in NM individuals but not in OC users. Cortical drive will be positively associated with circulating estradiol.
METHODS: Fourteen NM individuals and 11 OC users completed two time points (high hormone: NM mid-luteal, OC active pill and low hormone: NM early follicular, OC placebo). Hormone concentrations were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Quadriceps performance (isometric peak torque [PTISOM] and rate of torque development) was measured using an isokinetic dynamometer. Corticospinal excitability and intracortical excitability (short-interval intracortical inhibition [SICI] and intracortical facilitation) were assessed using transcranial magnetic stimulation. Linear mixed-effect models were used to examine hormone status, phase, and interaction effects. Linear regression determined associations between hormones, cortical drive, and strength.
RESULTS: There were no significant main effects or interactions for any cortical drive measure. There was a phase by hormone status interaction on the rate of torque development from 0 to 100 ms (RTD100), with a greater RTD100 at the high hormone phase than at the low hormone phase in the NM group but no difference between time points in the OC group. There was a main effect of phase on PTISOM, with a greater PTISOM at the low hormone phase regardless of hormone status. SICI was negatively associated with estradiol. RTD100 was positively associated with progesterone and moderated by hormone status.
CONCLUSIONS: MC phase did not impact cortical drive but did impact quadriceps performance. There were between-phase differences in speed of contraction among NM individuals but not among OC users. A higher progesterone level was associated with faster speed of contraction, especially among NM participants.
KEY CONCEPTS: (1)Corticospinal and intracortical excitability did not differ by menstrual cycle (MC) phase or oral contraceptive (OC) use.(2)Quadriceps rate of torque development was associated with progesterone concentration and varied across the MC, suggesting hormone expression influenced the rate of torque development (RTD) (speed of contraction).(3)The influence of endogenous ovarian hormones on RTD (speed of contraction) differed between OC users and naturally menstruating individuals.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: II.

title: Progression of peak athletic performance age in the past four decades.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older athletes are redefining the prime by extending their athletic longevity. A trend that women's peak performance age tends to increase, while men's remains largely unchanged, has been reported some time ago. The present study builds on this early work by examining more recent data to determine whether such gender differences persisted across contemporary periods and in different sporting events.
METHODS: Ages of Olympic medalists from 1984 to 2024 were analyzed as indicators of peak performance age (N.=2016).
RESULTS: In men, peak performance ages ranged 26±2 to 28±2 years in endurance, 26±2 to 27±2 years in power, 23±1 to 24±2 years in sprint, and 26±2 to 27±2 years in skill. In women, the ranges were from 27±2 to 29±2 years for endurance, 26±2 to 28±2 years for power, 23±2 to 24±2 years for sprint, and 23±3 to 26±3 years for skill. There were no gender differences in peak performance age among endurance, power, and sprint events in any era. However, in skill sports, male athletes demonstrated a higher peak performance age in 1984-1996 (P<0.05), a difference that has since disappeared. The age variabilities show an upward trend over time in both men and women.
CONCLUSIONS: We concluded that in recent years, both male and female athletes have achieved peak performance at comparable ages across all sport types.

title: Post-COVID-19 Penalty Trends Following an Injury-Prevention Rule Change in Rhode Island High School Boys' Hockey.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penalty infraction minute (PIM)-based rule modifications have been implemented in youth and high school ice hockey to reduce injury risk. A prior Rhode Island Interscholastic League (RIIL) study demonstrated a reduction in game-related injuries following implementation of a statewide 2015-2016 50/70 PIM rule. The durability of these behavioral trends post-COVID-19 has not been evaluated.
PURPOSE: This descriptive epidemiologic study evaluates post-pandemic trends in penalty infraction minutes and disqualifying penalties in RIIL boys' varsity ice hockey.
METHODS: Publicly available RIIL varsity boys' ice hockey data were reviewed for four consecutive seasons (2021-2022 through 2024-2025). Extracted variables included total rostered players, counts of players exceeding PIM thresholds (≥25, ≥50, ≥70), mean team PIM per game, goals scored, number of participating teams, and total disqualifying penalties per season. Data were summarized descriptively by season.
RESULTS: Across four seasons, rostered players ranged from 479 to 540, with 21 to 25 teams competing annually. Mean team PIM per game remained stable, ranging from 8.13 to 8.83. No players accumulated ≥50 or ≥70 PIM in any season. Players accumulating ≥25 PIM ranged from 17 to 24 per season. Disqualifying penalties occurred each season (range, 5-11 per year) without a consistent directional trend. Goals scored remained proportional to participating teams.
CONCLUSIONS: In post-pandemic seasons, PIM distributions and disqualifying penalties remained stable, with no recurrence of high-PIM accumulations requiring suspension. These findings suggest sustained behavioral patterns following rule modifications, but cannot be interpreted as evidence of injury reduction without injury surveillance data. Continued monitoring incorporating injury outcomes is warranted.

title: Atypical Suprasyndesmotic Distal Fibular Fracture in an Adolescent Athlete with Minimal Symptoms: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fractures of the distal fibula are common injuries in adolescent athletes, usually associated with identifiable trauma and rapid, uneventful healing. However, atypical mechanisms and minimal symptoms may obscure the diagnosis. We aim to describe the clinical course, imaging findings, and management of a suprasyndesmotic distal fibular fracture sustained during football practice, characterized by an unusual fracture mechanism without direct contact or major trauma and minimal clinical symptoms.
CASE REPORT: We present the case of a 15-year-old male admitted to the emergency department after an injury to the left leg while at a football practice. He reported missing the ball while attempting a shot and immediately perceived a crack in the kicking leg, without any collision or contact with another player. Clinical examination revealed painless palpation of both malleoli, varus stress testing, and isolated tenderness at the distal third of the fibula, without spontaneous pain.Radiographs confirmed a fracture located between the middle and distal thirds of the fibula, compatible with a suprasyndesmotic Weber C pattern. The lesion was non-displaced and initially described as a greenstick-type fracture. Conservative treatment with a plaster splint and non-weight-bearing was initiated. No analgesics were required.
CONCLUSION: Distal fibular fractures in young athletes may occur through unusual, contactless mechanisms with minimal symptoms, even in a suprasyndesmotic Weber C fracture pattern. Clinical assessment must remain the cornerstone of decision-making, while complementary imaging is useful to rule out complications, such as pseudarthrosis. Conservative management allowed full and safe return to sport in this patient after 4 months.

title: Flexible and stretchable bioelectronics for sports wearable monitoring: Materials, Device Engineering, and Intelligent Wearable Platforms.
abstract: Modern sports science is undergoing a paradigm shift from subjective coaching to objective, data-driven precision training. Consequently, wearable electronics for acquiring precise data during sports activities are attracting attention. However, conventional rigid wearables inherently suffer from mechanical mismatches between rigid wearables and the soft, deformable human skin, inducing severe motion artifacts and restricting natural biomechanics during high-intensity athletic activities. To address these limitations from a comprehensive perspective, this review systematically summarizes and analyzes recent advancements in next-generation flexible and stretchable bioelectronics tailored specifically for sports applications. We systematically examine the substrate materials, structural engineering designs, and device-level optimization strategies required to withstand repetitive strain, shear, and sweat-intensive environments. Building upon these conformable bio-interfaces, we discuss three core sensing modalities: electrochemical sensors for real-time analysis of sweat biomarkers, biophysical sensors for continuous electrophysiological and hemodynamic monitoring, and electromechanical sensors for high-fidelity kinematic and impact tracking. Furthermore, we discuss body-derived energy harvesting strategies to power sports wearables and wireless communication systems for continuous athletic monitoring. The importance of artificial intelligence and machine learning is increasing, as these techniques enable the removal of motion artifacts and facilitate objective analysis of athletic data for training and health monitoring applications. By evaluating targeted applications across aerobic and anaerobic exercise, cognitive state assessment, and post-exercise recovery, this review demonstrates how next-generation sports wearables contribute to the shift in sports science from reactive treatment toward proactive, data-driven performance enhancement and injury prevention.

title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
abstract: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HITblock) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V ˙ O 2 max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min-1 kg-1) were assigned to either HITblock or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HITblock completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity15-min), velocity at 4 mmol·L-1 blood lactate (velocity4mmol), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V ˙ O 2 max testing ( velocity V ˙ O 2 max ). HITblock demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocity V ˙ O 2 max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity4mmol (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity15-min did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HITblock compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

title: Gender Differences in Sports Injuries of the Foot and Ankle.
abstract: This article examines sex-based differences in foot and ankle injuries among female athletes, emphasizing the role of anatomic, hormonal, biomechanical, and sociocultural factors. Female athletes are disproportionately affected by ankle sprains, chronic instability, and bone stress injuries. Conditions such as relative energy deficiency in sport and the female athlete triad contribute to injury risk and long-term health consequences but remain under-recognized. This article highlights disparities in research, treatment, and outcomes, calling for improved screening, sex-specific prevention strategies, and greater inclusion of female subjects in sports medicine research to inform evidence-based care and optimize outcomes for female athletes.

title: Neuromuscular Fatigue and Recovery: Are Marathon and Trail Running Different?
abstract: Although trail and road are two running disciplines, they have distinct characteristics potentially leading to different physiological impacts that have never been examined. The aim of the present study was to compare neuromuscular fatigue and recovery between a marathon and two trail runs of equivalent effort (29 km; ± 1,400 m). Forty-one trained runners, specialized in either road or trail running, performed a simulated treadmill marathon (MARASIM), a simulated treadmill trail run (TRAILSIM), or a trail run in natural conditions (TRAILNAT), depending on their speciality. Neuromuscular fatigue, i.e. changes in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), voluntary activation (VA) and peak twitch (Tw) of the knee extensors (KE) and plantar flexors (PF), blood markers of muscle damage, jump performance, and force-velocity profile (FVP) were assessed before (PRE), immediately after (POST), one (+1 day), two (+2 days), and seven days (+7 days) following the runs. Muscle pain questionnaires were administered at PRE and during the month following the run. MARASIM showed significantly greater decreases in KE VA (-23.5% vs. -9.2% vs. -13.0%) and jump height (-11.7%; +11.4%; +5.9%, for squat jump), and significantly higher increases in blood markers of muscle damage (+1,726 UI.L -1; +641 UI.L -1; +363 UI.L -1; at +1 day) compared to TRAILSIM and TRAILNAT, respectively. The return to baseline occurred later in MARASIM for KE VA and jump height. Muscle soreness values also returned to baseline earlier in TRAILNAT and TRAILSIM compared to MARASIM. No differences between groups existed in KE Pt and MVC, in any PF neuromuscular fatigue variables, and FVP. Overall, marathon running appears to induce greater acute neuromuscular alterations than trail running, mostly on KE, with a slower return to baseline values.

title: The Sleep and Diet of Elite Female Australian Rules Football Athletes Differ With Age and Season Phase.
abstract: The Australian Football League Women's (AFLW) competition is comprised of a short, intensive competitive season, highlighting the importance of proper fuelling and recovery to support performance. Little is known about the dietary and sleep habits of AFLW athletes across a season, and the influence that age has on these behaviours. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effects of season phase and age on dietary intake and sleep in elite AFLW athletes. Dietary intake and sleep were assessed in 22 AFLW athletes (25.9 ± 5.0 y) over 10 nights, including five consecutive nights during both pre-season and in-season. Dietary intake was quantified through self-reported food diaries using a smartphone application (Easy Diet Diary), and sleep via a wearable monitoring device (Oura ring). Restricted maximum likelihood mixed models were used to determine variations in dietary intake and sleep in AFLW players between season phases (i.e., pre-season vs. in-season) and age. In-season protein (115.15 ± 35.14 vs. 126.48 ± 40.10 g, p = 0.026) and fat intakes (72.93 ± 29.55 vs. 83.43 ± 33.14 g, p = 0.012) were significantly lower compared to pre-season, with no differences in sleep measures observed between season phases. While age did not influence dietary intake, each additional year of age was associated with 8 min less sleep (p = 0.001) and 4 min earlier wake times (p = 0.032). These findings suggest that protein and fat intakes fluctuate across the seasons, with increasing age being a non-modifiable risk factor for shorter sleep durations within AFLW athletes.

title: Shoulder Arthritis.
abstract: Glenohumeral osteoarthritis is a common, debilitating joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss, subchondral bone remodeling, and capsular stiffness, leading to pain, restricted motion, and functional impairment. Diagnosis relies on both clinical evaluation and imaging studies. Classification systems, such as the Walch classification, assist in assessing disease severity and guiding treatment decisions. Management begins with conservative approaches, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and intra-articular injections, progressing to surgical interventions such as total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty for advanced disease. Early diagnosis and patient-specific treatment are essential to ensuring optimal patient outcomes.

title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model.
METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring.
RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded.
RESULTS: There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4).
CONCLUSION: We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats is partially mediated by enhancing necroptosis via phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study links Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1)-sensitive receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-associated signaling with biochemical, histological, inflammatory, and functional outcomes after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. Nec-1 reduced RIPK1 and MLKL phosphorylation, muscle injury, and early functional impairment. These findings extend prior skeletal-muscle studies by integrating molecular pathway activation with longitudinal functional recovery while supporting a contribution of RIPK1-associated necroptotic signaling.

title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy for Rapid Screening of S1-Class Anabolic Agents.
abstract: The abuse of S1-class anabolic agents poses significant health threats to athletes and is strictly prohibited by World Anti-Doping Organization (WADA). In this study, we developed a surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) method based on silver coated gold nanostars (GNS@Ag) core-shell nanoparticles for the rapid screening of four representative S1 agents: danazol, fluoxymesterone, zilpaterol, and androsterone. The synthesized nanomaterials feature sharp plasmonic hotspots that afford substantial SERS signal enhancement, enabling detection limits as low as~10-5 to ~10-7 g/mL. Owing to the fingerprint specificity of Raman spectroscopy, the method distinguishes different analytes and their mixtures by characteristic peak patterns. Coupled with principal component analysis (PCA), the approach enables robust discrimination of anabolic agents. Successful application to spiked milk samples demonstrates good recovery, rapid response, and practical utility, highlighting the potential of this SERS strategy as a promising tool for on-site anti-doping screening.

title: Gene amplification during differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells towards chondrocytes.
abstract: For decades, gene amplification was described as an attribute of tumor cells and as a physiological mechanism to increase gene copy numbers for the higher protein demand during the development of amphibians and flies. Notably, gene amplification has since been detected in normal mammalian cells during differentiation. Numerous amplified genes detected in tumor cells overlap with amplified genes detected during stem cell differentiation. Since stem cells have a valuable potency in regenerative therapies and since cartilage regeneration is a highly demanded therapeutic strategy, the current study investigated gene amplification dynamics during the chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Using quantitative PCR, copy number changes were analyzed for genes previously implicated in differentiation, as well as genes amplified in chondrosarcoma, including CDK4, MDM2, AGAP2, CPT1B, SHANK3, TRIB1 and MYC. Amplifications were transient and stage-specific: CDK4, CPT1B and SHANK3 exhibited the highest copy number increases at day 2, followed by a gradual decline by day 7, whereas AGAP2 and MDM2 increased later in differentiation. Laser microdissection of toluidine blue-stained areas revealed heterogeneity in amplification patterns: CDK4 amplification was prominent in areas lacking or showing moderate proteoglycan deposition; CPT1B amplification occurred in regions with absent, moderate or intense proteoglycan deposition; and SHANK3 amplification was restricted to areas with intense proteoglycan deposition. Notably, regions with the strongest proteoglycan staining exhibited no gene amplification, suggesting that gene amplification is an early, transient event that diminishes as differentiation progresses. These findings highlight gene amplification as a mechanism during chondrogenesis, potentially critical for early differentiation stages and genome stability in mature cells.

title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Application of FTIR to detect changes in blood plasma during a pre-competition period in a professional heavyweight boxer.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES AND DESIGN: This exploratory single-case study examined whether repeated attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy of blood plasma is technically feasible during a short pre-competition period and whether spectral regions co-vary with conventionally assayed biochemical markers.
METHODS: One professional heavyweight boxer was monitored over a 13-day pre-competition period characterized by reduced training load (tapering). Morning fasting blood was collected on five occasions (10, 13, 17, 20, and 23 May 2024) into lithium-heparin tubes and centrifuged to obtain plasma. Creatine kinase (CK), C-reactive protein (CRP), glucose, cortisol, testosterone, total and reduced glutathione, malondialdehyde, and zinc were quantified by conventional laboratory assays; ATR-FTIR spectra were acquired separately from the same plasma aliquots and were not used to quantify any of these analytes. Each plasma sample was measured eight times, yielding 40 spectra from five biological observations; the technical replicates are presented to illustrate within-sample visual consistency. Associations between the intensities of 22 spectral peaks and 12 biochemical variables were explored using Pearson correlation.
RESULTS: Plasma biochemical parameters showed changes during the pre-competition tapering period, including decreases in CK and CRP and increases in glutathione and testosterone, whereas cortisol remained relatively stable. FTIR spectra exhibited consistent vibrational profiles with changes in selected band intensities over time. Linear regression identified strong associations between glutathione levels and FTIR bands at 671, 699, and 721 cm-1 (R 2 = 0.80-0.92), as well as between cortisol and the 3,009 cm-1 band (R 2 = 0.77). Because of the limited number of observations (n = 5), these findings are preliminary and require validation in larger cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Repeated plasma measurements using ATR-FTIR demonstrated technical feasibility and visual consistency during a short pre-competition period in the studied athlete, while identifying potential spectral regions worthy of further investigation. The obtained results should be treated as preliminary. However, they do not provide evidence that ATR-FTIR enables the quantitative determination of glutathione or cortisol, or that it can be used to assess an athlete's competitive readiness. Confirmation of such capabilities requires studies involving adequately large and diverse groups of participants.

title: Speed at the edge of stability: a recovery-limited model of metabolic flux in the cheetah.
abstract: The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) achieves unmatched terrestrial speed through anatomical and muscular specialization for explosive power. Its type IIX glycolytic muscle phenotype, phosphocreatine (PCr) buffering and rapid glycolysis supply adenosine triphosphate at exceptionally high rates. This design enables acceleration but carries a metabolic cost: PCr is depleted, inorganic phosphate (Pi) and proton balance are disturbed, lactate is redistributed, and glucose and glycogen are used. We propose that feeding ecology may add to this cost. After a successful hunt, a substantial carcass meal imposes a second load through gastric acid secretion, the alkaline tide, pancreatic and biliary bicarbonate flux, bile acid signalling, and amino acid and lipid processing. Recovery starts when the chase ends, but its components resolve at different rates. PCr resynthesis and lactate transport may begin within minutes, whereas acid-base and electrolyte normalization, glycogen replenishment and intermediary-metabolite clearance may take longer. Feeding may therefore begin while slower recovery processes remain active, allowing the two loads to overlap. The model predicts that shorter hunt-to-feed or inter-meal intervals will increase the magnitude, duration or cumulative carry-over of acid-base, electrolyte and metabolomic perturbations. Direct cheetah evidence includes the fast-glycolytic muscle phenotype, high spot urinary creatinine concentrations, abundant urinary organic acids and altered acylcarnitine profiles. The timing and interaction of sprint recovery, digestion and metabolite clearance remain unmeasured. This Perspective integrates the adaptations that permit exceptional speed with their potential metabolic costs and provides a testable framework for evaluating how feeding ecology and managed feeding schedules influence recovery.

title: Periostin regulation by CEBPB and RACK1 and the effects of periostin-rich exosomes in osteoarthritis models.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves chondrocyte stress and disrupted intercellular communication, but the proteins associated with synovial fluid-derived exosomes remain incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVES: We investigated periostin regulation in chondrocyte models and cellular responses relevant to OA following exposure to periostin-rich exosomes.
METHODS: Exosomes isolated from synovial fluid samples from 15 patients with OA and 5 healthy volunteers (K-L grade 0) were analyzed using label-free proteomics. Human cartilage single-cell transcriptomic data, chondrocyte stress and serial-passage models, promoter-reporter assays, co-immunoprecipitation, protein-turnover assays, RNA sequencing, pathway-inhibition experiments, and destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) studies were used for follow-up.
RESULTS: Exploratory proteomics identified periostin as a candidate protein, whose abundance was also elevated in models associated with chondrocyte senescence. CEBPB increased periostin expression and POSTN promoter-reporter activity. RACK1 co-precipitated with periostin; RACK1 overexpression slowed periostin degradation and reduced its ubiquitination. Periostin-rich exosomes increased chondrocyte catabolic activity and senescence-associated changes, increased macrophage inflammatory markers, and increased endothelial cell migration and tube formation in vitro. In DMM mice, intra-articular delivery of short hairpin RNA (shRNA) constructs targeting Cebpb or Rack1 reduced cartilage damage, whereas periostin-rich exosome supplementation partially attenuated these effects. Representative joint-tissue immunoblots showed lower CEBPB or RACK1 expression in the corresponding shRNA groups and higher periostin abundance following exosome supplementation. A p38 inhibitor or a MEK/ERK inhibitor partially attenuated chondrocyte responses to exosome treatment.
CONCLUSION: CEBPB promotes periostin expression, whereas RACK1 increases periostin protein stability and contributes to p38/ERK-associated responses to periostin-rich exosomes in chondrocyte models. Intra-articular targeting of Cebpb or Rack1 reduced cartilage damage in DMM mice.

title: Metabolic Bone Health in Female Patients: Focus on Foot and Ankle.
abstract: Metabolic bone health is crucial for the overall well-being of female patients. Female athletes and young females are of particular interest, as their skeletal systems are still developing and are sensitive to the hormonal and physical stress of training and diet. Stress fractures occur with higher frequency in females with risk factors such as low bone mineral density (BMD). When low bone mineral density occurs along with menstrual irregularities and relative energy deficiency, it completes the female triad (23, 27, and 28). Any discussion of female BMD and metabolic bone health must include the female triad.

title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis.
abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

title: Age-Dependent Alterations in Glutathione Metabolites Following Muscle Injury.
abstract: Age-related impairments in antioxidant defences contribute to delayed tissue repair and increased susceptibility to oxidative stress following muscle injury. Glutathione (GSH), a key cellular antioxidant, plays a central role in redox homeostasis and recovery processes. GSH is synthesized through a sequential process involving glutamic acid and cysteine, catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to form γ-glutamyl cysteine (γGC), which subsequently combines with glycine to produce GSH. Using metabolomic profiling and acute skeletal muscle injury in mice, this study characterized age-dependent alterations in GSH biosynthesis. Clustering analysis identified that muscle from 12-month-old mice have a delayed GSH synthesis profile in response to injury compared to 3-month-old mice, with an age-dependent delay in γGC accumulation. This suggests that aging negatively influences metabolite profiles within the GSH synthesis pathway. As γGC lies downstream of this enzymatic step, its supplementation may bypass the GCL bottleneck. To test this, C2C12 myoblasts were treated with γGC (from 1-100 µg/mL), however this did not affect myoblast proliferation or differentiation. These data suggest detrimental age-related dysregulation of GSH-related metabolites in skeletal muscle repair, particularly γGC, however further examination of the role of exogenous γGC supplementation in this process is required to identify further therapeutic benefit.

title: Extracellular Vesicles Shed from Senescent Neonatal Pulmonary Microvascular Endothelial Cells Contribute to Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are critical mediators of intercellular communication but their role in bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) complicated by pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) is unclear. Here we test the hypothesis that hyperoxia induces neonatal pulmonary microvascular endothelial cell (PMEC) senescence and that EVs shed from these cells potentiate pulmonary vascular remodeling. Newborn PMECs exposed to 75% O2 had increased expression of senescence markers and young adult rats exposed to neonatal hyperoxia showed increased p16, p21 and p53 expression in pulmonary endothelial cells. In vivo, EVs isolated from the supernatant of senescent PMECs (senescent EVs) induced pulmonary vascular remodelling and PH in newborn rats. miRNA (miR) sequencing revealed 31 differentially expressed miRs in senescent EVs as compared to control EVs. Top upregulated miRs included miR-421, miR-4508, and miR-3960. Senescent EVs differentially regulated 271 genes in the lungs of newborn rats. The most downregulated gene was myocyte enhancer binding factor-2 (MEF2C), a known miR-421 target, involved in smooth cell plasticity. To further interrogate the mechanisms by which senescent EVs induce vascular remodelling, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMs) were incubated with control and senescent EVs, and smooth muscle cell phenotype was assessed. Senescent EVs down-regulated MEF2C and induced a synthetic PASM phenotype. EV uptake inhibition and miR-421 antagomir partially restored MEF2C expression and attenuated these changes. Together, these findings demonstrate that hyperoxia induces PMEC senescence and EVs shed from these senescent cells deliver a miR-421-MEF2C signal that potentiates pulmonary vascular remodelling. Strategies targeting this axis may have important implications for the treatment of BPD-PH.

title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.

title: Evaluation of a four-herb Chinese medicine formula at different concentrations on muscle damage and inflammation in a rat model of DOMS.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) impairs exercise recovery, while current treatments remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas may provide safe, multi-target interventions.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the dose-dependent protective effects of a four-herb Chinese medicine formulation (safflower, Chinese Angelica, peach kernel and myrrh) against DOMS in a rat model.
METHODS: Thirty-two male SPF SD rats were randomly allocated to control or low- (1696 mg/kg), medium- (3392 mg/kg), or high-dose (6784 mg/kg) groups. The formulation was administered orally for 11 days, with DOMS induced by exhaustive swimming on day 8. Serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 were measured at baseline and at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h post-exercise.
RESULTS: The medium- and high-dose groups exhibited significantly lower serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 levels than controls, with the high-dose group showing the largest reductions. The low-dose group showed limited or no significant reductions in most markers, demonstrating a clear dose-dependent protective effect.
CONCLUSIONS: The formulation dose-dependently attenuates muscle damage and inflammation in a rat DOMS model, with high-dose treatment achieving the fastest recovery. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm the efficacy and safety in humans.

title: Grading the evidence for sex-specific VO2max adaptation: An evidence-stratified narrative review of central, peripheral, and pulmonary determinants.
abstract: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) strongly predicts all-cause mortality, yet the step limiting it shifts along the oxygen transport cascade, and women remain underrepresented in the literature underpinning exercise guidelines. This narrative review integrates the mechanistic determinants of VO2max, examines how the rate-limiting step shifts with training status, modality, environment, and biological sex, and-as its principal contribution-systematically grades the evidence for sex-specific adaptation as established, emerging, or speculative. Convective oxygen delivery predominates in untrained individuals, whereas a substantial proportion of elite athletes develop exercise-induced arterial hypoxemia (EIAH) reflecting pulmonary diffusion limitation. Women's lower absolute VO2max is largely explained by blood volume and oxygen-carrying capacity. Sex differences in the magnitude of central cardiac remodeling are meta-analytically supported, but the proposed time-course difference rests on a single small cohort (n = 12), and peripheral-dominant adaptation derives from limited samples. Recent direct comparisons of EIAH between sexes conflict, and menstrual-cycle phase has at most a small effect on aerobic performance. Where evidence is strongest, sex-stratified interpretation is defensible; where weakest, individualized approaches remain a research direction. Adequately powered, sex-stratified, methodologically standardized studies are the field's most pressing need.

title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

title: Relative assessment of strontium-zinc-phosphate chemical conversion coatings on titanium for augmenting bioactivity: Effect of microstructure.
abstract: Titanium (Ti) and its alloy are widely used in orthopedics and dentistry implants because of their excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility. However, the bioinert surface of Ti implants may lead to osseointegration defects, which requires surface modification to resolve. In this work, bio-functional strontium zinc phosphate coatings denoted as SZP (SrZn2(PO4)2) with varying pattern and microstructure are controllably prepared on Ti surfaces via the phosphate chemical conversion (PCC) method. Although distinct micro/nano topographies of coatings can modulate osteoblast responses, the interaction between the micromorphology of Ti-based PCC coatings and osteoblasts remains elusive. To further explore this issue, the biological response of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) on SZP coatings with different microstructure is investigated in this study. The EDS and XRD results show that all the SZP coatings have similar phase composition. In addition, the SZP coating with lamellar structure presents better hydrophilicity and ion release characteristics comparing with that coating with block crystals. In vitro studies demonstrate that both SZP coatings have biocompatibility with BMSCs and significantly enhance cell adhesion, proliferation and differentiation comparing with bare Ti. Specifically, SZP coating with lamellar grains is more beneficial to the early osseointegration. This study shows that optimizing the microstructure of the PCC coating on Ti-based implants is one of the promising strategies for improving their bone integration.

title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model.
abstract: Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80-200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

title: Delphinidin induces the upregulation of miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle and miR-23a-3p release from intestinal cells.
abstract: Delphinidin, one of the major anthocyanidins, inhibits disuse muscle atrophy by increasing the expression of miR-23a-3p in mouse skeletal muscle. However, delphinidin is less stable and poorly absorbed in vivo, so its mechanism of function remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which delphinidin increases miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle. miRNAs can be packaged into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and secreted from cells. We investigated whether delphinidin induces the release of miR-23a-3p encapsulated in EVs from intestinal cells and whether these EVs increase miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle cells. A single dose of delphinidin increased the expression of miR-23a-3p in the small intestine of mice. To examine whether delphinidin affects the secretion of miR-23a-3p in intestinal cells, we used differentiated Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model. Results showed that delphinidin increases the expression of miR-23a-3p in EVs secreted from differentiated Caco-2 cells. In addition, EVs derived from delphinidin-treated Caco-2 cells were taken up by differentiated C2C12 myotubes, resulting in increased intracellular miR-23a-3p expression. Our in vitro results suggest that intestinal cell-derived EVs may contribute to the antimuscle atrophy activity of delphinidin through the delivery of miR-23a-3p to skeletal muscle cells.
